title: Python Programming
description: Beginner-to-advanced Python reference covering syntax, values, collections, functions, typing, iterators, classes, dataclasses, exceptions, context managers, modules, packaging, I/O, concurrency, testing, performance, and security.

sections.title: Syntax, Values & Control Flow
sections.description: Use Python's object model, truth rules, and structured control flow explicitly.

subtopics.title: Names, Objects, Equality & Identity
subtopics.description: Assignment binds a name to an object; it does not copy. == compares values, is compares identity and should normally be used only for singletons such as None.

codeBlocks.code:
items = [1, 2]
alias = items
copy = items.copy()
alias.append(3)
assert items == [1, 2, 3]
assert alias is items
assert copy == [1, 2] and copy is not items

value = None
if value is None: ...

callouts.title: Mutable Default and Aliasing Bugs Share a Cause
callouts.text: Several names can reference the same mutable object. Copy or publish immutable values when ownership must be independent.

subtopics.title: Numbers, Strings, Bytes & f-Strings
subtopics.description: int has arbitrary precision; float is binary floating point; str is Unicode text; bytes is binary data. Use Decimal for decimal policy and explicit encodings at boundaries.

codeBlocks.code:
from decimal import Decimal
price = Decimal('19.99')
quantity = 3
message = f'{quantity=} total={price * quantity:.2f}'

text = 'café'
data = text.encode('utf-8')
assert data.decode('utf-8') == text

callouts.title: Never Construct Decimal from float
callouts.text: Decimal(0.1) preserves the binary approximation. Parse decimal strings/integers and define rounding/quantization as domain policy.

subtopics.title: Conditions, Loops & Pattern Matching
subtopics.description: Use truthiness and short-circuiting carefully; for iterates; loop else runs only without break; match destructures values with ordered guarded cases.

codeBlocks.code:
match event:
    case {'type': 'payment', 'amount': amount} if amount > 0:
        process_payment(amount)
    case {'type': 'cancel', 'order_id': str(order_id)}:
        cancel(order_id)
    case _:
        raise ValueError(f'unsupported event: {event!r}')

for item in items:
    if predicate(item): break
else:
    handle_no_match()

callouts.title: Empty and Missing May Differ
callouts.text: if value treats 0, false, empty containers, and None alike. Use is None or explicit checks when those states have different meaning.

sections.title: Collections & Comprehensions
sections.description: Choose containers by ordering, uniqueness, lookup, mutability, and algorithmic needs.

subtopics.title: list, tuple, set, frozenset & dict
subtopics.description: Lists are mutable sequences; tuples immutable records/sequences; sets unique hashable values; dicts insertion-ordered key/value mappings.

table.title: Python Built-in Collection Selection
rows: Hashable set or immutable membership group

codeBlocks.code:
numbers = [3, 1, 3]
point = (10, 20)
unique = {3, 1, 3}
permissions = frozenset({'read', 'write'})
user_by_id = {'u1': {'name': 'Ada'}}

first, *middle, last = numbers
merged = defaults | overrides

callouts.title: Keys Must Be Hash-Stable
callouts.text: Dict/set keys must be hashable and their hash/equality-relevant state must not change while stored. Prefer immutable IDs, strings, tuples, or frozen dataclasses.

subtopics.title: Comprehensions & Generator Expressions
subtopics.description: Comprehensions eagerly build containers; generator expressions produce lazily. Keep transformations readable and free of side effects.

callouts.title: Split Complex Comprehensions
callouts.text: Multiple nested loops/conditions or mutation hide intent. Use named helpers and an ordinary loop when it improves debugging or error handling.

subtopics.title: Sorting, Grouping & Complexity
subtopics.description: sorted returns a stable list; key runs once per element. Use set/dict for average constant-time membership/indexing and itertools/collections for specialized operations.

codeBlocks.code:
from collections import Counter, defaultdict, deque
ordered = sorted(users, key=lambda u: (u.team, u.name.casefold()))
counts = Counter(word.casefold() for word in words)
groups = defaultdict(list)
for user in users: groups[user.team].append(user)
queue = deque(tasks); task = queue.popleft()

callouts.title: Avoid Quadratic Membership
callouts.text: Filtering a large list with x in another list is O(n×m). Convert the lookup side to set/dict when semantics allow.

sections.title: Functions, Closures & Typing
sections.description: Design explicit function contracts and use typing to communicate, not replace runtime validation.

subtopics.title: Parameters, Defaults, *args & **kwargs
subtopics.description: Use / for positional-only and * for keyword-only boundaries; defaults evaluate once at definition time.

callouts.title: Mutable Default Gotcha
callouts.text: Never use [] or {} as a default when calls need independent values. Use None or a sentinel, then allocate inside.

subtopics.title: First-Class Functions, Closures & Decorators
subtopics.description: Functions can be passed/stored/returned; closures capture bindings; decorators wrap definitions and should preserve metadata/signatures.

callouts.title: Decorator Semantics Must Match
callouts.text: A sync wrapper cannot transparently wrap async/generator/context-manager behavior. Preserve exceptions, cancellation, descriptor binding, and introspection.

subtopics.title: Type Hints, Protocols & Generics
subtopics.description: Annotations support static tools and documentation; Protocol expresses structural roles; generics preserve relationships between input and output types.

callouts.title: Typing Is Not Runtime Validation
callouts.text: External JSON, CLI, database, and network values still require validation/parsing. Avoid Any at boundaries because it disables useful checking transitively.

sections.title: Iteration, Generators & Resource Context
sections.description: Stream values lazily and make cleanup deterministic.

subtopics.title: Iterable vs Iterator
subtopics.description: An iterable creates an iterator; an iterator yields with __next__ until StopIteration and is normally one-pass.

callouts.title: Do Not Reuse Exhausted Iterators
callouts.text: Generators and file objects are iterators. Convert to a collection only when bounded, or call the iterable factory again for a new pass.

subtopics.title: yield, yield from & Generator Cleanup
subtopics.description: A generator suspends local state between yields; yield from delegates iteration and return handling; finally runs when exhausted/closed/collected subject to ownership.

callouts.title: Lazy Resource Lifetime Can Surprise
callouts.text: If a generator owns a file/socket, early exit may delay cleanup unless caller closes it. Prefer a context-managed iterable API for critical resources.

subtopics.title: with, Context Managers & ExitStack
subtopics.description: Context managers pair acquisition and release across success/failure. contextmanager simplifies one-resource flows; ExitStack manages dynamic sets.

callouts.title: Do Not Suppress Unexpected Exceptions
callouts.text: __exit__ returning true suppresses an exception. Do so only for explicitly handled types; preserve BaseException behavior for cancellation/interrupt/system exit.

sections.title: Classes, Dataclasses & Data Model
sections.description: Use classes for cohesive state/behavior and special methods to integrate with Python protocols.

subtopics.title: Classes, Instance/Class State & Composition
subtopics.description: Instance attributes belong to each object; class attributes are shared. Prefer composition for replaceable collaborators and shallow inheritance for true substitutable specialization.

callouts.title: Shared Mutable Class Attributes
callouts.text: A class-level list/dict is shared by every instance. Initialize per-instance mutable state in __init__ or dataclass default_factory.

subtopics.title: Dataclasses, Frozen Values & Enum
subtopics.description: Dataclasses generate value-oriented boilerplate; frozen improves assignment immutability; slots can reduce memory; Enum models a fixed named set.

callouts.title: Frozen Is Shallow
callouts.text: A frozen dataclass can still contain a mutable list. Use immutable field types when hashability/value semantics matter.

subtopics.title: Special Methods, Properties & Descriptors
subtopics.description: Implement protocols such as repr, equality, hashing, iteration, containers, call, context, and numeric operations consistently; properties preserve attribute syntax around derived/validated access.

callouts.title: Equality and Hash Must Agree
callouts.text: Equal objects must have equal hashes. Mutable value-equality objects generally should not be hashable while mutation can affect equality.

sections.title: Exceptions, Modules & Packaging
sections.description: Create contextual failure boundaries and reproducible import/install behavior.

subtopics.title: Exceptions, Chaining & ExceptionGroup
subtopics.description: Catch only failures you can handle, raise domain-specific errors with context, preserve causes, and use ExceptionGroup/except* for unrelated concurrent failures.

callouts.title: Never Use Bare except to Continue
callouts.text: It catches KeyboardInterrupt/SystemExit and can hide corrupted state. Catch specific Exception subclasses, log context, and re-raise when no safe recovery exists.

subtopics.title: Modules, Packages, Imports & __main__
subtopics.description: A module is executed once per interpreter/import cache; packages organize modules; absolute imports clarify project boundaries; main guard separates importable API from script entry.

callouts.title: Import-Time Side Effects
callouts.text: Do not open network connections, start threads, parse environment unpredictably, or perform migrations at import. Imports should be fast, deterministic, and safe for tools/tests.

subtopics.title: Virtual Environments, pyproject.toml & Builds
subtopics.description: Use an isolated environment, declare metadata/dependencies/build backend in pyproject, lock applications with one tool, and test built wheel/sdist artifacts.

codeBlocks.code:
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate        # Windows PowerShell: .venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
python -m pip install --upgrade pip
python -m pip install -e '.[dev]'
python -m build
python -m pip install dist/*.whl

callouts.title: Libraries and Applications Pin Differently
callouts.text: Libraries declare compatible ranges and test them; applications lock complete resolved versions for reproducible deployment. Avoid mixing global/system packages.

sections.title: I/O, Asyncio & Parallelism
sections.description: Select synchronous, threaded, asynchronous, or process execution from workload and cancellation needs.

subtopics.title: pathlib, Files, JSON & CSV
subtopics.description: Use pathlib for paths, context managers for files, explicit encoding/newline behavior, and schema validation for external structured data.

codeBlocks.code:
from pathlib import Path
import json
path = Path('config/app.json')
with path.open(encoding='utf-8') as file:
    value = json.load(file)

temporary = path.with_suffix('.tmp')
temporary.write_text(json.dumps(value, indent=2), encoding='utf-8')
temporary.replace(path)

callouts.title: Untrusted Deserialization
callouts.text: Never unpickle untrusted data. Limit sizes/depth, validate JSON/CSV fields, normalize allowed paths, and handle encoding/newline explicitly.

subtopics.title: asyncio, TaskGroup & Cancellation
subtopics.description: asyncio multiplexes cooperative I/O on an event loop. TaskGroup owns child tasks and groups failures; cancellation must propagate through cleanup.

codeBlocks.code:
import asyncio

async def load_all(urls: list[str]) -> list[bytes]:
    async with asyncio.TaskGroup() as group:
        tasks = [group.create_task(fetch(url), name=f'fetch:{url}') for url in urls]
    return [task.result() for task in tasks]

async def main():
    async with asyncio.timeout(10):
        return await load_all(urls)

asyncio.run(main())

callouts.title: Blocking Code Blocks the Event Loop
callouts.text: Use async-compatible libraries or asyncio.to_thread for bounded blocking I/O. CPU-heavy work belongs in processes/native code, not an async task.

subtopics.title: Threads, Processes & Shared State
subtopics.description: Threads suit blocking I/O/shared memory with synchronization; processes provide CPU parallelism/isolation with serialization and startup cost.

codeBlocks.code:
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor, ProcessPoolExecutor

with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=16) as pool:
    pages = list(pool.map(download, urls))

with ProcessPoolExecutor() as pool:
    hashes = list(pool.map(cpu_hash, files, chunksize=16))

callouts.title: The GIL Is Not a Data-Race Lock
callouts.text: Compound shared-state operations still require locks/queues/ownership and external resources have their own races. Free-threaded builds further require verified dependency/thread safety.

sections.title: Testing, Debugging, Performance & Security
sections.description: Make behavior deterministic and optimize from profiles rather than folklore.

subtopics.title: unittest, Fixtures & Test Doubles
subtopics.description: Test public behavior with deterministic inputs, temporary resources, and narrow fakes/mocks; always clean up through context or framework fixtures.

callouts.title: Patch Where Looked Up
callouts.text: If mocking, patch the symbol in the module under test, not its original definition module. Prefer dependency injection/fakes when interaction setup becomes brittle.

subtopics.title: Debugger, Logging & Profiling
subtopics.description: Use breakpoint, structured logging, traceback chaining, timeit, cProfile, tracemalloc, and production telemetry for evidence.

codeBlocks.code:
python -m pdb -m package.module
python -X dev -W error -m unittest
python -m cProfile -o profile.out -m package.module
python -m timeit 'sum(range(1000))'
python -X tracemalloc=25 -m package.module

callouts.title: Do Not Optimize Away Clarity Without Evidence
callouts.text: Profile representative workload. Algorithm/data-structure, I/O batching, database queries, and serialization often dominate syntax-level changes.

subtopics.title: Security & Production Checklist
subtopics.description: Review input, execution, dependencies, secrets, resource bounds, concurrency, and observability.

codeBlocks.code:
□ Supported Python version and dependencies are pinned for applications
□ External data is parsed/validated with size and depth limits
□ No eval/exec, unsafe pickle/YAML, shell=True, or string-built SQL on input
□ Paths are constrained to allowed roots
□ Secrets stay outside source, logs, tracebacks, and artifacts
□ Mutable defaults/shared state and aliasing are intentional
□ Files/connections/tasks/executors have deterministic cleanup
□ Async code contains no blocking work and propagates cancellation
□ Threads/processes have bounded concurrency and safe ownership
□ Exceptions preserve cause/context without leaking sensitive details
□ Built wheel/sdist and clean environment are tested
□ Logs, metrics, traces, profiling, health, and graceful shutdown exist

callouts.title: Patterns and FastAPI Are Separate
callouts.text: See Design Patterns with Python Examples for all 23 GoF patterns and FastAPI for HTTP validation, dependency injection, security, async request handling, and deployment.
